How we choose

Every place is recommended by named sources (review-aggregator star ratings never count as the recommender), pinned to its door from a published coordinate, and status-checked. Closed places stay, flagged, so you know they’re gone.

Must see
The places to plan a visit around — graded within each area, not across the city.
Worth the detour
Strong picks, worth going out of your way for.
Deep cut
For the curious: smaller, odder, more local.

Within each area, places are ordered by tier, then by number of named sources — never by popularity. Numbers on the cards match the pins on the map. No ratings, prices or opening hours are shown, because the guide doesn’t hold verified ones.

206 sights and 161 places to eat from the Loop out through the North, West and South Sides to the suburbs and the Indiana Dunes, each traceable to the source that named it. The architecture — the Rookery, Robie House, the river and the lakefront — anchors the map; the food runs on what Chicago does that nowhere else does: deep-dish and tavern-cut thin crust, Italian beef, the dragged-through-the-garden hot dog and the Maxwell Street Polish, the jibarito, mild-sauce chicken, the Rainbow Cone, and the immigrant corridors of Pilsen, Chinatown, Devon Avenue, Argyle and Little Village.

How this guide was made

How the cuisine filters were policed

Every food card names a specific dish — a cuisine label alone doesn’t qualify. Discovery started from what is unique to Chicago: deep-dish and tavern-style thin crust, Italian beef, the Chicago-style hot dog and the Maxwell Street Polish, the Puerto Rican jibarito, mild-sauce chicken and rib tips, the Rainbow Cone and Garrett popcorn — then the immigrant corridors: Pilsen and Little Village (Mexican), Chinatown, Devon Avenue (Indian & Pakistani), Argyle (Vietnamese), Ukrainian Village and the Polish Northwest Side, Swedish Andersonville. A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it happens to serve.

Web-searched, merit-measured and fact-checked

Every place is traceable to at least two credible sources — or one institutional authority (Michelin, James Beard, the National Park Service, UNESCO) — recorded in data/sources.json: the Chicago Tribune, Sun-Times, Chicago Magazine, Eater Chicago, The Infatuation, Block Club Chicago, WTTW, Time Out, Choose Chicago, Atlas Obscura and vetted creators (direct page fetches are blocked in the build environment, so sources were confirmed via search). Yelp and TripAdvisor never count. Every coordinate is verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked.
